title: The Tablet Wakes
hook: The tablet wakes mid-change. The Chorus wants a look.
scene: Wind on a Kent morning, left stalk already on, hole half-taken. The aftermarket tablet on the doghouse lights up — a familiar voice, a map, a lie. II-009's cousin. Eyes off a Beetle was bad. Eyes off the Ledger mid-change is how you write a sedan into the west-coast. The timeout is the look.
decision: The screen lights up in the middle of a lane change. Where do your eyes go?

options.text: Glance the screen — one second, then finish the change
options.result: One second is a room. The sedan was in it. You find him with the arm. The Chorus got the look it wanted.

options.text: Thumb the screen off while you steer — you can do two things
options.result: You steer with a thumb on glass. The hole moves. The Ledger does not. Two things was the problem.

options.text: Finish by memory — you already swept, the screen can wait
options.result: Memory is not a sweep. The room changed. You take a hole that closed. The tablet keeps talking to nobody.

options.text: Cancel the change, hold the lane, ignore the screen, sweep again, then move
options.result: You kill the stalk and let the tablet die alone. The hole you take later is one you have seen. The Chorus does not get a vote mid-change.

debrief: A screen mid-maneuver is a look you cannot afford. Cancel, hold, finish the driving, then the glass. The Chorus can wait.

source.psdp_skill: Skill nine: multi-lane roads – part one
source.teaching_target: Do not take eyes off the road to a screen during a lane change; cancel and complete the driving first.
